subject.title: [Feature]: GitHub Copilot provider cannot reach GitHub Enterprise data-residency (*.ghe.com) tenants

question: Should GitHub Enterprise data-residency routing be accepted inside the bundled github-copilot provider, or should it remain an external plugin/ClawHub direction?
rationale: Current main proves the bundled provider cannot route to *.ghe.com tenants, but the fix changes auth routing, token destination policy, and config/env behavior, so maintainer product and security intent are required before accepting the linked PR.

options.title: Accept narrow bundled-provider routing
options.body: Review and harden the linked PR so the existing github-copilot provider supports allowlisted github.com and single-label *.ghe.com hosts without changing public GitHub behavior.

options.title: Route to external plugin scope
options.body: Reject bundled-provider host routing and close this issue plus the linked PR with a clear statement that GHE Copilot must ship as a separate provider/plugin.

options.title: Require a generic host-routing API first
options.body: Keep the issue open but pause the linked PR until maintainers define a reusable provider-auth host-routing contract.

recommendation.title: Accept narrow bundled-provider routing
recommendation.body: Review and harden the linked PR so the existing github-copilot provider supports allowlisted github.com and single-label *.ghe.com hosts without changing public GitHub behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent current-main signal across the bundled Copilot provider/auth paths and adjacent provider work.
